article.title: Two hardening tools (AD+Windows) in ps1
article.summary: Hey, i'm working on those two little tools, any feedback is appreciated. ->>HostBadger, an open-source Windows hardening auditor in pure PowerShell. One read-only script takes a snapshot of each host, and you can push it through your EDR (CrowdStrike RTR or any tool that runs scripts) to a whole fleet in about 15 seconds per host. The analyzer then works offline and writes a clean HTML report with A–F scores, plus CSV and JSON Lines for your SIEM. - 138 checks: credentials, Defender and EDR, network exposure and NTLM relay paths, privilege escalation, logging, BitLocker - 1475 DISA STIG rules plus the CIS benchmark of each host's own Windows version, with the value found next to the value required - Vulnerable drivers (LOLDrivers), end-of-life and outdated software (endoflife.date), CISA KEV matches - Read-only by design, with a safety script that checks this from the code. No network unless you ask. What it can't read is "not evaluated", never clean. - Reversible fix scripts with rollback, and an optional AI summary where names become tokens before anything is sent Nothing to install (PowerShell 5.1 or 7): https://github.com/g4bri-3l3/HostBadger & ->>IDWolf: my own AD/Entra ID hardening tool that tells you whether your domain can be taken, and through which real-world attacks. Open-source, pure PowerShell, read-only collection (native cmdlets only), offline analysis. objectives.falsification_criterion: If a sweep of webroots and IIS/Apache process trees finds no anomalous children (cmd, powershell, /bin/sh) on Microsoft 365 / Entra ID hosts, post-exploit foothold is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where parent in ('w3wp.exe','httpd','nginx','java') and child in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','/bin/sh','/bin/bash')

objectives.title: Honeypot / canary check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If exposed canary instances of the same product show no probing or exploitation telemetry, opportunistic mass-exploitation against the org is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: canary_events | where product == '<product>' | where event_type in ('probe','exploit') | summarize by src_ip

hypotheses.title: Outbound C2 beaconing to reported infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: Hosts in the estate are beaconing to the command-and-control infrastructure reported in this article (domains, IPs, TLS fingerprints, or RMM tooling).
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'c2_beacon' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2025-24054, CVE-2025-33073; vectors: phishing, exploit, cloud-misconfig; impact: fraud; products: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID.

objectives.title: DNS resolution sweep for published C2 domains
objectives.falsification_criterion: If recursive DNS logs show zero resolutions for the IOC domains in the last 90 days, active beaconing is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: dns | where query in ('endoflife.date') | summarize count() by client_ip

objectives.title: Egress connections to published C2 IPs
objectives.falsification_criterion: If proxy / firewall egress logs show no connections to the IOC IPs or matching ASNs, network-level C2 is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: egress | where dst_ip in ('the published C2 IPs') | summarize bytes_out = sum(bytes_sent) by src_ip

objectives.title: Beacon periodicity / jitter analysis
objectives.falsification_criterion: If beacon-style periodic outbound connections (low jitter, small payloads) to uncategorised destinations are absent, covert C2 is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: conn | summarize stddev_interval = stdev(diff(ts)), count() by src_ip, dst_host | where count() > 50 and stddev_interval < 5s

objectives.title: TLS / JA3 fingerprint pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If JA3/JA3S fingerprints associated with the reported family are absent in TLS telemetry, encrypted C2 attribution is weakened.
objectives.suggested_query: tls | where ja3 in (ti_lookup('family','ja3')) | summarize by src_ip, sni

objectives.title: Remote-monitoring tooling abuse check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If unmanaged AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installs are absent, RMM-based C2 is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where name in ('anydesk.exe','teamviewer.exe','screenconnect.exe','atera*.exe') and signer != 'corp_managed'

hypotheses.title: Identity compromise of privileged users
hypotheses.statement: Privileged identities have been compromised through phishing, MFA fatigue, help-desk social engineering, or OAuth illicit-consent grants.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'identity_compromise' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2025-24054, CVE-2025-33073; vectors: phishing, exploit, cloud-misconfig; impact: fraud; products: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID.

objectives.title: Impossible-travel / atypical sign-ins
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra ID / Okta risky-sign-in detections show no impossible-travel hits on privileged identities, account compromise is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: signin | where risk_level in ('high','medium') and user in (privileged_users) | summarize by country, ip

objectives.title: MFA-fatigue / push-bombing
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MFA telemetry shows no bursts of denied pushes followed by a successful one for the same user, MFA-fatigue compromise is disproven.

objectives.title: Help-desk social-engineering pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If ticketing / call-recording shows no recent password-reset or MFA-reset requests for privileged users without proper verification, help-desk vector is unsupported.

objectives.title: OAuth illicit-consent grants

Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies. CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets. Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies. Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. CISA also recommends users take the following measures to protect themselves from social engineering attacks: Do not click web links or open attachments in unsolicited email messages. Refer to Recognizing and Avoiding Email Scams for more information on avoiding email scams. Refer to Avoiding Social Engineering and Phishing Attacks for more information on social engineering attacks. No known public exploitation specifically targeting these vulnerabilities has been reported to CISA at this time. article.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday for October 2026 — Snort rules and prominent vulnerabilities
article.summary: Blog post covering the vulnerabilities disclosed during Microsoft Patch Tuesday.
article.raw_text: Microsoft Patch Tuesday for October 2026 — Snort rules and prominent vulnerabilities Blog post covering the vulnerabilities disclosed during Microsoft Patch Tuesday. Microsoft has released its monthly security update for October 2026, which includes 1415 vulnerabilities affecting a range of products, including 85 that Microsoft marked as "critical." Microsoft notes that 1 of the vulnerabilities disclosed this month have been exploited in the wild CVE-2026-96951 is a security feature bypass vulnerability that affects Windows Shell. The shared weakness is Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection'). The vulnerability has a CVSS base score of 8.8. Out of 85 "critical" vulnerabilities, 67 are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities. Microsoft considers exploitation of the following vulnerabilities more likely. CVE-2026-70229 is a remote code execution vulnerability that affects Windows Active Directory Domain Services. The shared weakness is Incorrect Authorization. The vulnerability has a CVSS base score of 8.1. CVE-2026-70571 is a remote code execution vulnerability that affects Microsoft Exchange Server. The shared weakness is Stack-based Buffer Overflow. The vulnerability has a CVSS base score of 8.1. Microsoft considers exploitation of the following vulnerabilities less likely. CVE-2026-105733 , CVE-2026-102214 , and CVE-2026-108399 affect Windows Hyper-V. CVE-2026-105733 has an impact of remote code execution; involves Incorrect Initialization of Resource; has a CVSS base score of 8.8. CVE-2026-102214 has an impact of remote code execution; involves Use After Free; has a CVSS base score of 8.8. CVE-2026-108399 has an impact of elevation of privilege; involves Heap-based Buffer Overflow; has a CVSS base score of 7.2. CVE-2026-100202 is a remote code execution vulnerability that affects Windows Message Queuing Queue Manager. The shared weakness is Use After Free. The vulnerability has a CVSS base score of 9.8. CVE-2026-100209 , CVE-2026-100210 , CVE-2026-100211 , CVE-2026-97739 , CVE-2026-97745 , CVE-2026-97755 , CVE-2026-97759 , CVE-2026-97765 , CVE-2026-97778 , CVE-2026-97741 , CVE-2026-97742 , CVE-2026-97753 , CVE-2026-97756 , CVE-2026-97758 , CVE-2026-97761 , CVE-2026-97767 , CVE-2026-97776 , and CVE-2026-97780 are remote code execution vulnerabilities that affect Microsoft Office Excel. Each has a CVSS base score of 8.8. CVE-2026-100209 , CVE-2026-100211 , CVE-2026-97745 , and CVE-2026-97759 involve Use After Free. CVE-2026-100210 , CVE-2026-97765 , CVE-2026-97756 , CVE-2026-97758 , CVE-2026-97776 , and CVE-2026-97780 involve Heap-based Buffer Overflow. CVE-2026-97739 involves Heap-based Buffer Overflow and Integer Underflow (Wrap or Wraparound). CVE-2026-97755 involves Out-of-bounds Read. CVE-2026-97778 involves Integer Overflow or Wraparound. CVE-2026-97741 involves Heap-based Buffer Overflow and Off-by-one Error. CVE-2026-97742 involves Stack-based Buffer Overflow. CVE-2026-97753 involves Heap-based Buffer Overflow and Integer Overflow or Wraparound. CVE-2026-97761 involves Stack-based Buffer Overflow. CVE-2026-97767 involves Double Free and NULL Pointer Dereference. CVE-2026-100215 is a remote code execution vulnerability that affects Microsoft Graphics Component. The shared weakness is Heap-based Buffer Overflow. The vulnerability has a CVSS base score of 7.8. CVE-2026-100219 and CVE-2026-105016 are remote code execution vulnerabilities that affect Microsoft QUIC. Each has a CVSS base score of 9.8. CVE-2026-100219 involves Use After Free. CVE-2026-105016 involves Heap-based Buffer Overflow. CVE-2026-100220 is a remote code execution vulnerability that affects Windows Media Video Decoder. The shared weakness is Heap-based Buffer Overflow. The vulnerability has a CVSS base score of 8.8. CVE-2026-102211 , CVE-2026-88074 , CVE-2026-108130 , CVE-2026-108471 , and CVE-2026-96914 are elevation of privilege vulnerabilities that affect Windows Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) Enclave. CVE-2026-102211 involves Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition') and Use After Free; has a CVSS base score of 7.0. CVE-2026-88074 involves Integer Overflow or Wraparound; has a CVSS base score of 7.8. CVE-2026-108130 involves Heap-based Buffer Overflow; has a CVSS base score of 7.8. CVE-2026-108471 involves Untrusted Pointer Dereference; has a CVSS base score of 8.8. CVE-2026-96914 involves Heap-based Buffer Overflow and Integer Overflow or Wraparound; has a CVSS base score of 8.8. hypotheses.title: Initial access via CVE-2026-96951 affecting Microsoft Exchange
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor has attempted to obtain initial access to our environment by exploiting CVE-2026-96951 in Microsoft Exchange within the last 30 days.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'initial_access_cve' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-96951, CVE-2026-70229, CVE-2026-70571; vectors: exploit, rdp; products: Microsoft Exchange, Active Directory, Linux kernel.

objectives.title: Inventory exposure to Microsoft Exchange
objectives.falsification_criterion: If zero internet-facing assets run a vulnerable build of Microsoft Exchange, the external-exploitation hypothesis is disproven for CVE-2026-96951.
objectives.suggested_query: asset_inventory | where product == 'Microsoft Exchange' and exposure == 'internet' and version in (vulnerable_versions)

objectives.title: Hunt for exploit attempts at the edge
objectives.falsification_criterion: If WAF / firewall / IDS show no exploit-signature hits for CVE-2026-96951 in the last 30 days, in-the-wild exploitation against us is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: edge_logs | where signature contains 'CVE' or uri matches /exploit-pattern-for-CVE-2026-96951/ | summarize count() by src_ip, dst_host

objectives.title: Patch-status correlation
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MDM / patch-management shows 100% deployment of the CVE-2026-96951 fix across exposed hosts, the hypothesis is disproven by remediation.
objectives.suggested_query: patch_state | where kb in (fixes_for('CVE-2026-96951')) | summarize coverage = avg(installed) by host_role

objectives.title: Post-exploit web-shell sweep
objectives.falsification_criterion: If a sweep of webroots and IIS/Apache process trees finds no anomalous children (cmd, powershell, /bin/sh) on Microsoft Exchange hosts, post-exploit foothold is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where parent in ('w3wp.exe','httpd','nginx','java') and child in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','/bin/sh','/bin/bash')

objectives.title: Honeypot / canary check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If exposed canary instances of the same product show no probing or exploitation telemetry, opportunistic mass-exploitation against the org is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: canary_events | where product == '<product>' | where event_type in ('probe','exploit') | summarize by src_ip

hypotheses.title: Outbound C2 beaconing to reported infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: Hosts in the estate are beaconing to the command-and-control infrastructure reported in this article (domains, IPs, TLS fingerprints, or RMM tooling).
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'c2_beacon' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-96951, CVE-2026-70229, CVE-2026-70571; vectors: exploit, rdp; products: Microsoft Exchange, Active Directory, Linux kernel.

objectives.title: DNS resolution sweep for published C2 domains
objectives.falsification_criterion: If recursive DNS logs show zero resolutions for the IOC domains in the last 90 days, active beaconing is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: dns | where query in ('snort.org') | summarize count() by client_ip

objectives.title: Egress connections to published C2 IPs
objectives.falsification_criterion: If proxy / firewall egress logs show no connections to the IOC IPs or matching ASNs, network-level C2 is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: egress | where dst_ip in ('the published C2 IPs') | summarize bytes_out = sum(bytes_sent) by src_ip

objectives.title: Beacon periodicity / jitter analysis
objectives.falsification_criterion: If beacon-style periodic outbound connections (low jitter, small payloads) to uncategorised destinations are absent, covert C2 is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: conn | summarize stddev_interval = stdev(diff(ts)), count() by src_ip, dst_host | where count() > 50 and stddev_interval < 5s

objectives.title: TLS / JA3 fingerprint pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If JA3/JA3S fingerprints associated with the reported family are absent in TLS telemetry, encrypted C2 attribution is weakened.
objectives.suggested_query: tls | where ja3 in (ti_lookup('family','ja3')) | summarize by src_ip, sni

objectives.title: Remote-monitoring tooling abuse check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If unmanaged AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installs are absent, RMM-based C2 is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where name in ('anydesk.exe','teamviewer.exe','screenconnect.exe','atera*.exe') and signer != 'corp_managed'

hypotheses.title: Identity compromise of privileged users
hypotheses.statement: Privileged identities have been compromised through phishing, MFA fatigue, help-desk social engineering, or OAuth illicit-consent grants.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'identity_compromise' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-96951, CVE-2026-70229, CVE-2026-70571; vectors: exploit, rdp; products: Microsoft Exchange, Active Directory, Linux kernel.

objectives.title: Impossible-travel / atypical sign-ins
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra ID / Okta risky-sign-in detections show no impossible-travel hits on privileged identities, account compromise is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: signin | where risk_level in ('high','medium') and user in (privileged_users) | summarize by country, ip

objectives.title: MFA-fatigue / push-bombing
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MFA telemetry shows no bursts of denied pushes followed by a successful one for the same user, MFA-fatigue compromise is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: mfa | summarize denies = countif(result=='deny'), accepts = countif(result=='accept') by user, bin(ts,1h) | where denies > 5 and accepts > 0

objectives.title: Help-desk social-engineering pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If ticketing / call-recording shows no recent password-reset or MFA-reset requests for privileged users without proper verification, help-desk vector is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: tickets | where action in ('password_reset','mfa_reset') and target in (privileged_users) | join (verifications) on ticket_id

objectives.title: OAuth illicit-consent grants
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra/Workspace audit logs show no recently consented third-party apps with high-impact scopes, OAuth abuse is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: audit | where action == 'Consent to application' and scopes contains 'Mail.Read' or 'files.read.all'

article.title: Satel Netco Design
article.summary: View CSAF Summary Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary scripts in a user's browser, consume excessive system resources, enumerate files, create or modify files, and potentially execute arbitrary code. The following versions of Satel Netco Design are affected: Satel Netco Design CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 8.8 Satel Satel Netco Design 3 Vulnerabilities Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting'), Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity, Relative Path Traversal Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Communications Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Finland Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-105269 Satel Netco Design versions prior to v2.1.7 contains a stored cross site scripting vulnerability. An authenticated user with Network Operator privileges could store untrusted content that is rendered without adequate neutralization. Successful exploitation could allow script execution in another user's browser when the affected content is viewed. Read More 1 Affected Product Satel Satel Netco Design: Product Status: known_affected Remediations Vendor fix Satel advises users to update to Satel Netco Design v2.1.7. Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 6.8 MEDIUM CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H 4.0

hypotheses.title: Initial access via CVE-2026-105269 affecting the affected product/service
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor has attempted to obtain initial access to our environment by exploiting CVE-2026-105269 in the affected product/service within the last 30 days.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'initial_access_cve' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-105269, CVE-2026-104628, CVE-2026-105275; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: Inventory exposure to the affected product
objectives.falsification_criterion: If zero internet-facing assets run a vulnerable build of the affected product, the external-exploitation hypothesis is disproven for CVE-2026-105269.
objectives.suggested_query: asset_inventory | where product == 'the affected product' and exposure == 'internet' and version in (vulnerable_versions)

objectives.title: Hunt for exploit attempts at the edge
objectives.falsification_criterion: If WAF / firewall / IDS show no exploit-signature hits for CVE-2026-105269 in the last 30 days, in-the-wild exploitation against us is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: edge_logs | where signature contains 'CVE' or uri matches /exploit-pattern-for-CVE-2026-105269/ | summarize count() by src_ip, dst_host

objectives.title: Patch-status correlation
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MDM / patch-management shows 100% deployment of the CVE-2026-105269 fix across exposed hosts, the hypothesis is disproven by remediation.
objectives.suggested_query: patch_state | where kb in (fixes_for('CVE-2026-105269')) | summarize coverage = avg(installed) by host_role

objectives.title: Post-exploit web-shell sweep
objectives.falsification_criterion: If a sweep of webroots and IIS/Apache process trees finds no anomalous children (cmd, powershell, /bin/sh) on the affected product hosts, post-exploit foothold is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where parent in ('w3wp.exe','httpd','nginx','java') and child in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','/bin/sh','/bin/bash')

objectives.title: Honeypot / canary check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If exposed canary instances of the same product show no probing or exploitation telemetry, opportunistic mass-exploitation against the org is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: canary_events | where product == '<product>' | where event_type in ('probe','exploit') | summarize by src_ip

hypotheses.title: Outbound C2 beaconing to reported infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: Hosts in the estate are beaconing to the command-and-control infrastructure reported in this article (domains, IPs, TLS fingerprints, or RMM tooling).
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'c2_beacon' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-105269, CVE-2026-104628, CVE-2026-105275; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: DNS resolution sweep for published C2 domains
objectives.falsification_criterion: If recursive DNS logs show zero resolutions for the IOC domains in the last 90 days, active beaconing is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: dns | where query in ('www.cisa.gov') | summarize count() by client_ip

objectives.title: Egress connections to published C2 IPs
objectives.falsification_criterion: If proxy / firewall egress logs show no connections to the IOC IPs or matching ASNs, network-level C2 is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: egress | where dst_ip in ('the published C2 IPs') | summarize bytes_out = sum(bytes_sent) by src_ip

objectives.title: Beacon periodicity / jitter analysis
objectives.falsification_criterion: If beacon-style periodic outbound connections (low jitter, small payloads) to uncategorised destinations are absent, covert C2 is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: conn | summarize stddev_interval = stdev(diff(ts)), count() by src_ip, dst_host | where count() > 50 and stddev_interval < 5s

objectives.title: TLS / JA3 fingerprint pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If JA3/JA3S fingerprints associated with the reported family are absent in TLS telemetry, encrypted C2 attribution is weakened.
objectives.suggested_query: tls | where ja3 in (ti_lookup('family','ja3')) | summarize by src_ip, sni

objectives.title: Remote-monitoring tooling abuse check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If unmanaged AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installs are absent, RMM-based C2 is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where name in ('anydesk.exe','teamviewer.exe','screenconnect.exe','atera*.exe') and signer != 'corp_managed'

hypotheses.title: Identity compromise of privileged users
hypotheses.statement: Privileged identities have been compromised through phishing, MFA fatigue, help-desk social engineering, or OAuth illicit-consent grants.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'identity_compromise' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-105269, CVE-2026-104628, CVE-2026-105275; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: Impossible-travel / atypical sign-ins
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra ID / Okta risky-sign-in detections show no impossible-travel hits on privileged identities, account compromise is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: signin | where risk_level in ('high','medium') and user in (privileged_users) | summarize by country, ip

objectives.title: MFA-fatigue / push-bombing
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MFA telemetry shows no bursts of denied pushes followed by a successful one for the same user, MFA-fatigue compromise is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: mfa | summarize denies = countif(result=='deny'), accepts = countif(result=='accept') by user, bin(ts,1h) | where denies > 5 and accepts > 0

objectives.title: Help-desk social-engineering pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If ticketing / call-recording shows no recent password-reset or MFA-reset requests for privileged users without proper verification, help-desk vector is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: tickets | where action in ('password_reset','mfa_reset') and target in (privileged_users) | join (verifications) on ticket_id

objectives.title: OAuth illicit-consent grants
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra/Workspace audit logs show no recently consented third-party apps with high-impact scopes, OAuth abuse is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: audit | where action == 'Consent to application' and scopes contains 'Mail.Read' or 'files.read.all'

hypotheses.title: Initial access via CVE-2026-100730 affecting the affected product/service
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor has attempted to obtain initial access to our environment by exploiting CVE-2026-100730 in the affected product/service within the last 30 days.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'initial_access_cve' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-100730, CVE-2026-105281, CVE-2026-85479; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: Inventory exposure to the affected product
objectives.falsification_criterion: If zero internet-facing assets run a vulnerable build of the affected product, the external-exploitation hypothesis is disproven for CVE-2026-100730.
objectives.suggested_query: asset_inventory | where product == 'the affected product' and exposure == 'internet' and version in (vulnerable_versions)

objectives.title: Hunt for exploit attempts at the edge
objectives.falsification_criterion: If WAF / firewall / IDS show no exploit-signature hits for CVE-2026-100730 in the last 30 days, in-the-wild exploitation against us is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: edge_logs | where signature contains 'CVE' or uri matches /exploit-pattern-for-CVE-2026-100730/ | summarize count() by src_ip, dst_host

objectives.title: Patch-status correlation
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MDM / patch-management shows 100% deployment of the CVE-2026-100730 fix across exposed hosts, the hypothesis is disproven by remediation.
objectives.suggested_query: patch_state | where kb in (fixes_for('CVE-2026-100730')) | summarize coverage = avg(installed) by host_role

objectives.title: Post-exploit web-shell sweep
objectives.falsification_criterion: If a sweep of webroots and IIS/Apache process trees finds no anomalous children (cmd, powershell, /bin/sh) on the affected product hosts, post-exploit foothold is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where parent in ('w3wp.exe','httpd','nginx','java') and child in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','/bin/sh','/bin/bash')

objectives.title: Honeypot / canary check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If exposed canary instances of the same product show no probing or exploitation telemetry, opportunistic mass-exploitation against the org is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: canary_events | where product == '<product>' | where event_type in ('probe','exploit') | summarize by src_ip

hypotheses.title: Outbound C2 beaconing to reported infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: Hosts in the estate are beaconing to the command-and-control infrastructure reported in this article (domains, IPs, TLS fingerprints, or RMM tooling).
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'c2_beacon' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-100730, CVE-2026-105281, CVE-2026-85479; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: DNS resolution sweep for published C2 domains
objectives.falsification_criterion: If recursive DNS logs show zero resolutions for the IOC domains in the last 90 days, active beaconing is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: dns | where query in ('www.cisa.gov') | summarize count() by client_ip

objectives.title: Egress connections to published C2 IPs
objectives.falsification_criterion: If proxy / firewall egress logs show no connections to the IOC IPs or matching ASNs, network-level C2 is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: egress | where dst_ip in ('the published C2 IPs') | summarize bytes_out = sum(bytes_sent) by src_ip

objectives.title: Beacon periodicity / jitter analysis
objectives.falsification_criterion: If beacon-style periodic outbound connections (low jitter, small payloads) to uncategorised destinations are absent, covert C2 is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: conn | summarize stddev_interval = stdev(diff(ts)), count() by src_ip, dst_host | where count() > 50 and stddev_interval < 5s

objectives.title: TLS / JA3 fingerprint pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If JA3/JA3S fingerprints associated with the reported family are absent in TLS telemetry, encrypted C2 attribution is weakened.
objectives.suggested_query: tls | where ja3 in (ti_lookup('family','ja3')) | summarize by src_ip, sni

objectives.title: Remote-monitoring tooling abuse check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If unmanaged AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installs are absent, RMM-based C2 is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where name in ('anydesk.exe','teamviewer.exe','screenconnect.exe','atera*.exe') and signer != 'corp_managed'

hypotheses.title: Identity compromise of privileged users
hypotheses.statement: Privileged identities have been compromised through phishing, MFA fatigue, help-desk social engineering, or OAuth illicit-consent grants.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'identity_compromise' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-100730, CVE-2026-105281, CVE-2026-85479; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: Impossible-travel / atypical sign-ins
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra ID / Okta risky-sign-in detections show no impossible-travel hits on privileged identities, account compromise is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: signin | where risk_level in ('high','medium') and user in (privileged_users) | summarize by country, ip

objectives.title: MFA-fatigue / push-bombing
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MFA telemetry shows no bursts of denied pushes followed by a successful one for the same user, MFA-fatigue compromise is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: mfa | summarize denies = countif(result=='deny'), accepts = countif(result=='accept') by user, bin(ts,1h) | where denies > 5 and accepts > 0

objectives.title: Help-desk social-engineering pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If ticketing / call-recording shows no recent password-reset or MFA-reset requests for privileged users without proper verification, help-desk vector is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: tickets | where action in ('password_reset','mfa_reset') and target in (privileged_users) | join (verifications) on ticket_id

objectives.title: OAuth illicit-consent grants
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra/Workspace audit logs show no recently consented third-party apps with high-impact scopes, OAuth abuse is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: audit | where action == 'Consent to application' and scopes contains 'Mail.Read' or 'files.read.all'

article.title: HMS Networks PEAK-System PCAN Windows drivers
article.summary: View CSAF Summary Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could crash the Windows kernel. The following versions of HMS Networks PEAK-System PCAN Windows drivers are affected: PEAK-System Device Driver Setup PCAN Windows CAN device drivers CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 7.1 HMS Networks PEAK-System Device Driver Setup 5 Vulnerabilities Out-of-bounds Write, Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow'), Improper Validation of Array Index, Untrusted Pointer Dereference, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Transportation Systems, Healthcare and Public Health, Energy, Critical Manufacturing Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Sweden Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-109576 The parser in PEAK-System PCAN driver correctly detected the malformed record, but the loop iterating the record list advanced its processed-bytes counter even when a record had been rejected as invalid. Read More 2 Affected Products HMS Networks PEAK-System Device Driver Setup: Product Status: known_affected Remediations Mitigation HMS Networks AB has addressed the issue in version 5.1.4 and recommends that users upgrade to the newest available version. Users can find software updates for PEAK-System PCAN on the software download page. Mitigation For more information see the associated HMS security advisory. HMS Networks PCAN Windows CAN device drivers: Product Status: known_affected Remed

Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as virtual private networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies. CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets. Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies. Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. CISA also recommends users take the following measures to protect themselves from social engineering attacks: Do not click web links or open attachments in unsolicited email messages. Refer to Recognizing and Avoiding Email Scams for more information on avoiding email scams. Refer to Avoiding Social Engineering and Phishing Attacks for more information on social engineering attacks. No known public exploitation specifically targeting these vulnerabilities has been reported to CISA at this time. These vulnerabilities are not exploitable remotely. objectives.suggested_query: canary_events | where product == '<product>' | where event_type in ('probe','exploit') | summarize by src_ip

hypotheses.title: Identity compromise of privileged users
hypotheses.statement: Privileged identities have been compromised through phishing, MFA fatigue, help-desk social engineering, or OAuth illicit-consent grants.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'identity_compromise' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-109576, CVE-2026-101103, CVE-2026-94188; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: Impossible-travel / atypical sign-ins
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra ID / Okta risky-sign-in detections show no impossible-travel hits on privileged identities, account compromise is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: signin | where risk_level in ('high','medium') and user in (privileged_users) | summarize by country, ip

objectives.title: MFA-fatigue / push-bombing
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MFA telemetry shows no bursts of denied pushes followed by a successful one for the same user, MFA-fatigue compromise is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: mfa | summarize denies = countif(result=='deny'), accepts = countif(result=='accept') by user, bin(ts,1h) | where denies > 5 and accepts > 0

objectives.title: Help-desk social-engineering pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If ticketing / call-recording shows no recent password-reset or MFA-reset requests for privileged users without proper verification, help-desk vector is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: tickets | where action in ('password_reset','mfa_reset') and target in (privileged_users) | join (verifications) on ticket_id

objectives.title: OAuth illicit-consent grants
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra/Workspace audit logs show no recently consented third-party apps with high-impact scopes, OAuth abuse is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: audit | where action == 'Consent to application' and scopes contains 'Mail.Read' or 'files.read.all'

hypotheses.title: Outbound C2 beaconing to reported infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: Hosts in the estate are beaconing to the command-and-control infrastructure reported in this article (domains, IPs, TLS fingerprints, or RMM tooling).
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'c2_beacon' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-109576, CVE-2026-101103, CVE-2026-94188; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: DNS resolution sweep for published C2 domains
objectives.falsification_criterion: If recursive DNS logs show zero resolutions for the IOC domains in the last 90 days, active beaconing is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: dns | where query in ('the published C2 domains') | summarize count() by client_ip

objectives.title: Egress connections to published C2 IPs
objectives.falsification_criterion: If proxy / firewall egress logs show no connections to the IOC IPs or matching ASNs, network-level C2 is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: egress | where dst_ip in ('the published C2 IPs') | summarize bytes_out = sum(bytes_sent) by src_ip

objectives.title: Beacon periodicity / jitter analysis
objectives.falsification_criterion: If beacon-style periodic outbound connections (low jitter, small payloads) to uncategorised destinations are absent, covert C2 is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: conn | summarize stddev_interval = stdev(diff(ts)), count() by src_ip, dst_host | where count() > 50 and stddev_interval < 5s

objectives.title: TLS / JA3 fingerprint pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If JA3/JA3S fingerprints associated with the reported family are absent in TLS telemetry, encrypted C2 attribution is weakened.
objectives.suggested_query: tls | where ja3 in (ti_lookup('family','ja3')) | summarize by src_ip, sni

objectives.title: Remote-monitoring tooling abuse check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If unmanaged AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installs are absent, RMM-based C2 is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where name in ('anydesk.exe','teamviewer.exe','screenconnect.exe','atera*.exe') and signer != 'corp_managed'

article.title: Hitachi Energy RTU500 Product
article.summary: View CSAF Summary Hitachi Energy is aware of vulnerabilities that affect RTU500 product versions listed in this document. These vulnerabilities if exploited can have impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of the product. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions for information about the mitigation/remediation. The following versions of Hitachi Energy RTU500 Product are affected: RTU500 series CMU Firmware vers:RTU500_series_CMU_Firmware/>=13.5.1| =13.6.1| =13.7.1| =13.8.1| =12.7.1| CVSS Vendor Equipment v3 8.8 Hitachi Energy RTU500 series CMU Firmware 7 Vulnerabilities NULL Pointer Dereference, Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion'), Use After Free, Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information, Insufficiently Protected Credentials, Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay, Authentication Bypass by Primary Weakness Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Energy Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Switzerland Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-17539 RTU500 has a vulnerability, where high-load scenarios, such as sending GI requests at short intervals, may cause a NULL pointer dereference in the last entry of the enhanced message queue. This can cause a BCI_IEC104 fatal write error, resulting in connection interruption and restart, and ultimately a denial of service for bidirectional IEC 60870-5-104 communication. General Mitigation Factors Recommended security practices and firewall configurations can help protect a process control network from attacks that originate from outside the network. Such practices include that process control systems are physically protected from direct access by unauthorized personnel, have no direct connections to the Internet, and are separated from other networks by means of a firewall system that has a minimal number of ports exposed, and others that have to be evaluated case by case. Process control systems should not be used for Internet surfing, instant messaging, or receiving e-mails. Portable computers and removable storage media should be carefully scanned for viruses before they are connected to a control system. Proper password policies and processes should be followed. Additional information on Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices can be found in the Hitachi Energy “Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices” Cybersecurity Notification. [1] SSVC SSVCv2/E:N/A:N/2026-09-28T14:29:30Z/ Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the exploitation risk of this vulnerability. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from the internet. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most recent version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies. CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets. Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies. Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. hypotheses.title: Initial access via CVE-2026-17539 affecting the affected product/service
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor has attempted to obtain initial access to our environment by exploiting CVE-2026-17539 in the affected product/service within the last 30 days.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'initial_access_cve' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-17539, CVE-2026-28388, CVE-2026-6732; vectors: exploit, vpn-edge; impact: ddos.

objectives.title: Inventory exposure to the affected product
objectives.falsification_criterion: If zero internet-facing assets run a vulnerable build of the affected product, the external-exploitation hypothesis is disproven for CVE-2026-17539.
objectives.suggested_query: asset_inventory | where product == 'the affected product' and exposure == 'internet' and version in (vulnerable_versions)

objectives.title: Hunt for exploit attempts at the edge
objectives.falsification_criterion: If WAF / firewall / IDS show no exploit-signature hits for CVE-2026-17539 in the last 30 days, in-the-wild exploitation against us is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: edge_logs | where signature contains 'CVE' or uri matches /exploit-pattern-for-CVE-2026-17539/ | summarize count() by src_ip, dst_host

objectives.title: Patch-status correlation
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MDM / patch-management shows 100% deployment of the CVE-2026-17539 fix across exposed hosts, the hypothesis is disproven by remediation.
objectives.suggested_query: patch_state | where kb in (fixes_for('CVE-2026-17539')) | summarize coverage = avg(installed) by host_role

objectives.title: Post-exploit web-shell sweep
objectives.falsification_criterion: If a sweep of webroots and IIS/Apache process trees finds no anomalous children (cmd, powershell, /bin/sh) on the affected product hosts, post-exploit foothold is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where parent in ('w3wp.exe','httpd','nginx','java') and child in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','/bin/sh','/bin/bash')

objectives.title: Honeypot / canary check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If exposed canary instances of the same product show no probing or exploitation telemetry, opportunistic mass-exploitation against the org is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: canary_events | where product == '<product>' | where event_type in ('probe','exploit') | summarize by src_ip

hypotheses.title: Outbound C2 beaconing to reported infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: Hosts in the estate are beaconing to the command-and-control infrastructure reported in this article (domains, IPs, TLS fingerprints, or RMM tooling).
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'c2_beacon' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-17539, CVE-2026-28388, CVE-2026-6732; vectors: exploit, vpn-edge; impact: ddos.

objectives.title: DNS resolution sweep for published C2 domains
objectives.falsification_criterion: If recursive DNS logs show zero resolutions for the IOC domains in the last 90 days, active beaconing is disproven.

objectives.title: Egress connections to published C2 IPs
objectives.falsification_criterion: If proxy / firewall egress logs show no connections to the IOC IPs or matching ASNs, network-level C2 is unsupported.

objectives.title: Beacon periodicity / jitter analysis
objectives.falsification_criterion: If beacon-style periodic outbound connections (low jitter, small payloads) to uncategorised destinations are absent, covert C2 is unlikely.

article.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
article.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.
article.raw_text: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild. Expect to see quite a few websites serving “404” or “Page Not Found” errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild. Image: Shutterstock.com, Sashkin. The flaws at issue are present in PHP , the programming language that powers sites running on a large number of web publishing systems, including Drupal , Magento , Joomla and WordPress . Earlier today, PHP released an emergency security update to fix two critical bugs that can allow an attacker to execute code of their choosing on a vulnerable server. Reuters reports that government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline today after the PHP vulnerabilities were disclosed. Cloudflare said it has already detected some exploitation of the flaw, and that at 3:02 am (UTC) it implemented web application firewall rules to protect websites from attack traffic seeking to exploit the bugs, which could cause a denial of service condition, remote code execution, and data exposure. OpenAI , which was involved in the vulnerability research and outreach, said “given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory.” Security experts at Wiz said every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities [full disclosure: Wiz is an advertiser on this blog]. “These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history,” reads a blog post published today by a team of researchers at Wiz, which was one of several organizations credited with discovering the vulnerabilities. “The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.” The Wiz researchers say it is likely the PHP vulnerabilities will be mass-exploited to install web-based backdoors or “web shells,” which give attackers a web-based panel that allows them to remotely control infected sites. Wiz said that prior to the PHP bugs being publicly disclosed, the company worked with the PHP team, Calif and OpenAI to measure the size of the problem and coordinate patch verification and disclosure. The PHP zero-day vulnerabilities are being tracked by their CVE numbers, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 , and they affect all web servers running PHP 5.4 or later. The bugs are fixed in PHP 8.5.12 , 8.4.27 , 8.3.36 , and 8.2.35 . According to Wiz, PHP is so deeply embedded in many web applications that we are likely to see organizations struggling to patch these vulnerabilities for some time to come, comparing this PHP vulnerability pair with the Log4Shell weakness that emerged in 2021 — a widespread, severe-as-it-gets security flaw in Log4j, a popular Java logging framework. “A vulnerability in core PHP reaches far beyond a single application,” the Wiz researchers wrote. “PHP runs across clouds, hosting providers, content-delivery networks and millions of independently managed servers. Reducing exposure before the technical details became public required coordinated work across that entire ecosystem.” The SANS Internet Storm Center is keeping an eye on major software platforms that are shipping updates to deal with these PHP flaws. For example, Ubuntu just released updated PHP packages. This is a fast-moving story. Updates will be noted here with timestamps.

article.title: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates
article.summary: Cisco Talos is aware of eight intermediate certificates belonging to the intermediate certificate authority, eMudhra.
article.raw_text: Compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates Cisco Talos is aware of eight intermediate certificates belonging to the intermediate certificate authority, eMudhra. Cisco Talos is aware of eight intermediate certificates belonging to the intermediate certificate authority, eMudhra . Rather than possessing the mandatory 384 bits of pseudo-random security, several private keys evaluated single-digit and double-digit integers. This misconfiguration allows an attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs to impersonate any website or service. Six of the TLS certificates, trusted by Chrome, Mozilla, and Apple have been blocked by these vendors already. Two other certificates, used for codesigning by Microsoft, have also been blocked. Talos expects there will be additional patches available across a variety of technologies as software applications work to remediate the certificates’ exposure. Following the disclosure, eMudhra has revoked the compromised certificates and stopped issuing new certificates under its G3 root. Compromise details The cause of this issue, originated during an April 30, 2025 key generation activity conducted by eMudhra under its emSign Root TLS CA - G3 and cross-signed Comodo AAA Certificate Services. During a key generation ceremony for 24 subordinate CAs, a flaw in eMudhra’s key generation process created a second set of weak P-384 keys during a wrap/unwrap step. Those keys were mistakenly used for eight intermediate CA certificates. This flaw took the encryption from 384 bytes of entropy down to 3 – 8, making recovering the private keys trivial. The following are the impacted certificates, as illustrated in Mozilla’s bug report : EM EV TLS CA - G3B (eMudhra BV), CCADB A012304 SHA-256 E7568FE6E12331F4FD7DE61DA4C7559D0F8EB192A218D4741A3BA75184333838 serial c7c41efe92d825f05eae841a4a82c1, issuer emSign Root TLS CA - G3 EM OV TLS CA - G3B (eMudhra BV), CCADB A012308 SHA-256 98B896625C0C230ADEEC3EB2CF6AAD5001ECF9156A68644E82374CE5833BC25B serial 6cada367fb1c100088120ea202d568, issuer emSign Root TLS CA - G3 EM DV TLS CA - G3B (eMudhra BV), CCADB A012302 SHA-256 42C4ACCD12C4F59597925E1A08A7A90102608543809308D50EC427E118BA1493 serial a4aee678f23362b4c0e460b772f214, issuer emSign Root TLS CA - G3 EM EV TLS CA - G3C (eMudhra Inc), CCADB A012296 SHA-256 432EC25F0D28DE9006D97BF752F17BBB2CD41F669933FCB072D9A1148D0261F3 serial 8009928a64107601af05fa2f19f109, issuer emSign Root TLS CA - G3 EM OV TLS CA - G3C (eMudhra Inc), CCADB A012300 SHA-256 CB6E15165AC802E9B3F993F16C25D41F4E81C21EBDE71AE1B012AC00BF9C7C3F serial 296926c227a3a1526392b19482a504, issuer emSign Root TLS CA - G3 EM DV TLS CA - G3C (eMudhra Inc), CCADB A012294 SHA-256 0164D7CEAE5BB909C272AF151FF44B1177AE9B47D9424B94F1D9558C30934D19 serial 588b2e3c2bb8cda13e1a1209254321, issuer emSign Root TLS CA - G3 EM OV CS CA - G3B (eMudhra BV), CCADB A012306 SHA-256 9E39DE2881273ACC225A149C72BA3E0F51424963669AB633EE1DC7DF5DB067B4 serial 7818933f8f85b4619a2b35fba83d0a, issuer emSign Root CS CA - G3 EM OV CS CA - G3C (eMudhra Inc), CCADB A012298 SHA-256 4B2460A466F95FD40113BCDCCA2CEB29B3B093921DE45474DA7DF48874C630B1 serial 544b7f922c31ae220a4a922916f6e6, issuer emSign Root CS CA - G3 CVE-2026-111943 Unlike languages that defer entirely to external dynamic system libraries (like OpenSSL), the Go programming runtime implements its own X.509 chain verification engine in the standard library (crypto/x509). While Go usually queries platform certificates, several platforms or static container environments rely on embedded or legacy root certificate pools where certificate revocations are ignored. To eliminate exploitation across the entire cloud-native ecosystem including Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and Prometheus, the Go team designated the compromised certificates as a vulnerability, CVE-2026-111943, and released Go versions 1.27.3 and 1.26.10. The fixed versions filter out chains containingthe SHA-256 hashes of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) for all eight compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates. Impact These compromised certificates could allow adversaries to impersonate servers and intercept or modify traffic. The impact of their exposure is far more than just web browsers. Other programs that check for TLS certificates might still be impacted since they may not check revocation lists. One clear example is related to virtual private networks (VPNs); these technologies will likely require software updates to mitigate the issue. Based on this guidance, Talos strongly recommends users update software using and handling TLS certificates as fixes become available. Talos is actively monitoring the impact of these compromised certificates and has not seen any malicious incidents involving them in the wild yet (as of October 21, 2026 14:00 UTC / 10:00 a.m. ET). Significance of this breach Public key infrastructure relies on trust being delegated through certificate chains: root CAs authorize intermediate CAs, which can issue certificates within the scope of their authority. An attacker who obtains an intermediate CA’s private key may be able to issue fraudulent certificates that clients accept, subject to the intermediate certificate’s constraints and each client’s validation controls. In this incident, six compromised intermediates were for TLS and two were for code signing. For TLS, an attacker able to intercept or redirect a connection could use a fraudulent certificate to impersonate a server and potentially read or modify traffic if the client still trusts the affected key and no applicable protection blocks it. Protections such as revocation, key distrust, certificate transparency enforcement, and certificate pinning can prevent or expose such an attack. Browser vendors have blocked the affected TLS keys, but other applications may rely on separate trust stores or validation paths: Enterprise infrastructure and VPNs Organizations should assess TLS-using software and appliances, including proxies, reverse load balancers, VPN clients, and gateways. Exposure depends on the certificate chain being validated and the trust store and revocation behavior in use. A stale or separately managed trust store may need an application, operating-system, firmware, or trust-bundle update; verify the required action for each product. Software supply chains and CI/CD Build runners and package managers may be exposed if they fetch content over TLS while still trusting an affected key and an attacker can intercept the connection. A fraudulent TLS certificate could enable registry impersonation, but it would not by itself bypass separate package integrity checks, such as lockfile hashes, checksums, signatures, or provenance controls. Assess the actual package-manager configuration and dependency path. Industrial IoT and embedded systems Review devices that use bundled or independently managed CA stores, especially where certificate revocation or trust-store updates may be limited. Some devices may require a vendor update or compensating control, but the necessary action depends on each device’s validation and update mechanisms. Talos recommends updating affected software and trust stores as vendor fixes become available. Coverage The following SNORT® SIDs provide coverage for this threat: 67363 - 67374. Talos would like to highlight the efforts of Chris Morrison for providing emergency coverage and mitigations for this threat.

article.raw_text: Patch Tuesday - October 2026 Microsoft is publishing 1,413 own-product vulnerabilities on October 2026 Patch Tuesday , including 1,102 vulnerabilities in Windows. Anyone who enjoyed last month’s record-setting Patch Tuesday will love the October 2026 edition, because it’s much bigger still. As Rapid7 has noted over the course of 2026, there is every reason to suppose that vulnerability volumes will continue to rise. Microsoft is aware of exploitation in the wild for just one of the vulnerabilities published today, as well as public disclosure for two others. Windows Shell: zero-day security feature bypass The Windows Shell is Microsoft’s term for the GUI interaction logic for the entire OS provided by explorer.exe and associated libraries and APIs, and for the second time this year , the Windows Shell is the site of an exploited-in-the-wild zero-day vulnerability. Today’s specimen is CVE-2026-96951 . Once again, the immediate prize for an attacker is a Mark of the Web (MOTW) bypass. What this means is that Windows won’t provide the user with a dialog explaining that Windows protected their PC, because in this case, it didn’t. Exploitation requires that a user opens a specially crafted malicious file or visits an attacker-controlled site, so the evergreen advice about being careful what you click remains valid. Fans of vintage operating systems should note that Windows Server 2012 doesn’t receive a patch, although Server 2012 R2 does. The advisory acknowledges reporters from multiple organizations, although none from within Microsoft. The vulnerability also affected Microsoft’s Outlook.com cloud services, although Outlook.com was patched in a build dated several weeks ago. .NET Framework: zero-day security feature bypass Microsoft is aware of some level of public disclosure of CVE-2026-108398 , a .NET Framework security feature bypass. Exploitation requires an attacker with an existing foothold to register a malicious .NET assembly for loading by a protected process, bypassing Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) enforcement. Microsoft rebranded WDAC as App Control for Business several years ago, so you may know it under its new name. The Microsoft Learn page for Application Control for Windows points out that “your organization's data is one of its most valuable assets... and threat actors want it”, and this is, of course, correct. The patch presumably removes an attacker-controlled location from the list of places .NET Framework searches for registered assemblies, which are typically contained within DLLs and executables. If any further indications were needed that vulnerability volumes are increasing industry-wide, this is only the second month that Microsoft has published vulnerabilities with six-digit CVE numbers, but these extra-large CVEs will seem unremarkable from now on. Outlook: multiple no-interaction RCEs The sheer volume of vulnerabilities in recent Patch Tuesday releases can easily include several examples of potentially concerning vulnerabilities, each of which might have been more remarkable in its own right back when volumes were lower. Today, Microsoft has published five separate remote code execution vulnerabilities in Outlook where the preview pane is a vector, meaning that simply scrolling past an email in the Outlook reading pane would be sufficient to trigger exploitation. Worse still, Outlook might helpfully display the preview without any user interaction at all. All five of CVE-2026-70242 , CVE-2026-97749 , CVE-2026-97016 , CVE-2026-88156 , and CVE-2026-70291 receive fixes in the same patches. No-interaction Outlook preview pane vulnerabilities can sometimes feature prominently in state-backed actor campaigns, with CVE-2023-23397 as a prominent example in this category . Edge: security updates unclear In September 2026, Microsoft did not appear to publish any desktop browser security advisories between the start of the month and Patch Tuesday. In October, a slightly different approach has emerged: several recent entries in the Edge security updates release notes mention new versions of Edge which incorporate the latest updates from the Chromium project, but without detailing which vulnerabilities have been fixed, stating instead, “CVE's will be added as soon as available,” and directing readers to the Security Update Guide (SUG). At the time of writing, the SUG lists a total of zero vulnerabilities addressed in Edge in the first 13 days of October, and the “CVE’s added soon” message has been up for over a week. As a result, defenders have no obvious way of knowing which recent vulnerabilities Microsoft has addressed in Edge. Microsoft lifecycle update In Microsoft product lifecycle news, today sees Windows 11 24H2 Home & Pro reach end of servicing, while Windows Server 2022 moves to extended support, with free critical security updates continuing but no further feature development. Also this month, the final curtain falls for Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 with the expiry of the third and final year of cash-for-updates Extended Security Update (ESU) program for these aging workhorses. Microsoft lists the end of ESU Year 3 on October 14, 2026, in both cases. Microsoft has a long history of providing at least some security patches for products beyond the end of support, with Server 2008 being a case in point, but the time to move past Server 2012 is now. Office 2021 also moves into retirement on October 14; this includes the Long-Term Servicing Channel , with no ESU available in that case. Also on October 15, 2026, Exchange Server 2016 and Exchange Server 2019 finally join the “no ESU” club, after two previous six-month reprieves. Microsoft seems to really mean it this time, since any future Exchange Server CVEs released by MSRC will stop mentioning Exchange 2016 and 2019. However, Microsoft points out that a lack of warnings does not mean those unsupported versions are not vulnerable to future security issues. Summary charts

hypotheses.title: Initial access via CVE-2026-96951 affecting Microsoft Exchange
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor has attempted to obtain initial access to our environment by exploiting CVE-2026-96951 in Microsoft Exchange within the last 30 days.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'initial_access_cve' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-96951, CVE-2026-108398, CVE-2026-70242; vectors: exploit; impact: fraud; products: Microsoft Exchange.

objectives.title: Inventory exposure to Microsoft Exchange
objectives.falsification_criterion: If zero internet-facing assets run a vulnerable build of Microsoft Exchange, the external-exploitation hypothesis is disproven for CVE-2026-96951.
objectives.suggested_query: asset_inventory | where product == 'Microsoft Exchange' and exposure == 'internet' and version in (vulnerable_versions)

objectives.title: Hunt for exploit attempts at the edge
objectives.falsification_criterion: If WAF / firewall / IDS show no exploit-signature hits for CVE-2026-96951 in the last 30 days, in-the-wild exploitation against us is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: edge_logs | where signature contains 'CVE' or uri matches /exploit-pattern-for-CVE-2026-96951/ | summarize count() by src_ip, dst_host

objectives.title: Patch-status correlation
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MDM / patch-management shows 100% deployment of the CVE-2026-96951 fix across exposed hosts, the hypothesis is disproven by remediation.
objectives.suggested_query: patch_state | where kb in (fixes_for('CVE-2026-96951')) | summarize coverage = avg(installed) by host_role

objectives.title: Post-exploit web-shell sweep
objectives.falsification_criterion: If a sweep of webroots and IIS/Apache process trees finds no anomalous children (cmd, powershell, /bin/sh) on Microsoft Exchange hosts, post-exploit foothold is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where parent in ('w3wp.exe','httpd','nginx','java') and child in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','/bin/sh','/bin/bash')

objectives.title: Honeypot / canary check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If exposed canary instances of the same product show no probing or exploitation telemetry, opportunistic mass-exploitation against the org is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: canary_events | where product == '<product>' | where event_type in ('probe','exploit') | summarize by src_ip

hypotheses.statement: Hosts in the estate are beaconing to the command-and-control infrastructure reported in this article (domains, IPs, TLS fingerprints, or RMM tooling).

objectives.title: DNS resolution sweep for published C2 domains
objectives.falsification_criterion: If recursive DNS logs show zero resolutions for the IOC domains in the last 90 days, active beaconing is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: dns | where query in ('explorer.exe','outlook.com') | summarize count() by client_ip

objectives.title: Egress connections to published C2 IPs
objectives.falsification_criterion: If proxy / firewall egress logs show no connections to the IOC IPs or matching ASNs, network-level C2 is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: egress | where dst_ip in ('the published C2 IPs') | summarize bytes_out = sum(bytes_sent) by src_ip

objectives.title: Beacon periodicity / jitter analysis
objectives.falsification_criterion: If beacon-style periodic outbound connections (low jitter, small payloads) to uncategorised destinations are absent, covert C2 is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: conn | summarize stddev_interval = stdev(diff(ts)), count() by src_ip, dst_host | where count() > 50 and stddev_interval < 5s

objectives.title: TLS / JA3 fingerprint pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If JA3/JA3S fingerprints associated with the reported family are absent in TLS telemetry, encrypted C2 attribution is weakened.
objectives.suggested_query: tls | where ja3 in (ti_lookup('family','ja3')) | summarize by src_ip, sni

objectives.suggested_query: process | where name in ('anydesk.exe','teamviewer.exe','screenconnect.exe','atera*.exe') and signer != 'corp_managed'

article.title: CISA Urges Patching Newly Exploited Vulnerability in Ivanti Connect Secure
article.summary: CISA is aware of Ivanti’s disclosure of a newly exploited vulnerability, CVE-2026-104935 , affecting Ivanti Connect Secure versions 25.1.1.1 and prior, 25.1.2.2 and prior, and 22.8R2.4 and prior. CISA is aware of cyber threat actors exploiting this zero-day authentication bypass vulnerability, which allows remote, unauthenticated execution of arbitrary commands, to conduct credential theft and data exfiltration. CISA added CVE-2026-104935 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Oct. 13, 2026. CISA urges organizations with affected Ivanti Connect Secure appliances and deployments to immediately update to the latest version, as outlined in Ivanti’s Security Advisory Ivanti Connect Secure (CVE-2026-104935) . Organizations should also review the Ivanti Connect Secure 25.x Upgrade and Migration Compatibility Guide for detailed patching guidance for hardware and virtual appliance deployments. Ivanti Connect Secure version 22.8 reaches end of life on Jan. 31, 2027. Note: Ivanti’s Integrity Checker Tool may not detect evidence of exploitation of CVE-2026-104935 because threat actor commands execute in memory. If your organization suspects a compromise, CISA recommends implementing the following actions from Ivanti Connect Secure Recovery Procedures : Create a backup of the appliance configuration. CISA urges organizations with affected Ivanti Connect Secure appliances and deployments to immediately update to the latest version, as outlined in Ivanti’s Security Advisory Ivanti Connect Secure (CVE-2026-104935) . hypotheses.title: Initial access via CVE-2026-62927 affecting the affected product/service
hypotheses.statement: A threat actor has attempted to obtain initial access to our environment by exploiting CVE-2026-62927 in the affected product/service within the last 30 days.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'initial_access_cve' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-62927, CVE-2026-63252, CVE-2026-58080; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: Inventory exposure to the affected product
objectives.falsification_criterion: If zero internet-facing assets run a vulnerable build of the affected product, the external-exploitation hypothesis is disproven for CVE-2026-62927.
objectives.suggested_query: asset_inventory | where product == 'the affected product' and exposure == 'internet' and version in (vulnerable_versions)

objectives.title: Hunt for exploit attempts at the edge
objectives.falsification_criterion: If WAF / firewall / IDS show no exploit-signature hits for CVE-2026-62927 in the last 30 days, in-the-wild exploitation against us is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: edge_logs | where signature contains 'CVE' or uri matches /exploit-pattern-for-CVE-2026-62927/ | summarize count() by src_ip, dst_host

objectives.title: Patch-status correlation
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MDM / patch-management shows 100% deployment of the CVE-2026-62927 fix across exposed hosts, the hypothesis is disproven by remediation.
objectives.suggested_query: patch_state | where kb in (fixes_for('CVE-2026-62927')) | summarize coverage = avg(installed) by host_role

objectives.title: Post-exploit web-shell sweep
objectives.falsification_criterion: If a sweep of webroots and IIS/Apache process trees finds no anomalous children (cmd, powershell, /bin/sh) on the affected product hosts, post-exploit foothold is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where parent in ('w3wp.exe','httpd','nginx','java') and child in ('cmd.exe','powershell.exe','/bin/sh','/bin/bash')

objectives.title: Honeypot / canary check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If exposed canary instances of the same product show no probing or exploitation telemetry, opportunistic mass-exploitation against the org is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: canary_events | where product == '<product>' | where event_type in ('probe','exploit') | summarize by src_ip

hypotheses.title: Outbound C2 beaconing to reported infrastructure
hypotheses.statement: Hosts in the estate are beaconing to the command-and-control infrastructure reported in this article (domains, IPs, TLS fingerprints, or RMM tooling).
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'c2_beacon' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-62927, CVE-2026-63252, CVE-2026-58080; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: DNS resolution sweep for published C2 domains
objectives.falsification_criterion: If recursive DNS logs show zero resolutions for the IOC domains in the last 90 days, active beaconing is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: dns | where query in ('opcuaserverconfig.copy','www.cisa.gov') | summarize count() by client_ip

objectives.title: Egress connections to published C2 IPs
objectives.falsification_criterion: If proxy / firewall egress logs show no connections to the IOC IPs or matching ASNs, network-level C2 is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: egress | where dst_ip in ('the published C2 IPs') | summarize bytes_out = sum(bytes_sent) by src_ip

objectives.title: Beacon periodicity / jitter analysis
objectives.falsification_criterion: If beacon-style periodic outbound connections (low jitter, small payloads) to uncategorised destinations are absent, covert C2 is unlikely.
objectives.suggested_query: conn | summarize stddev_interval = stdev(diff(ts)), count() by src_ip, dst_host | where count() > 50 and stddev_interval < 5s

objectives.title: TLS / JA3 fingerprint pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If JA3/JA3S fingerprints associated with the reported family are absent in TLS telemetry, encrypted C2 attribution is weakened.
objectives.suggested_query: tls | where ja3 in (ti_lookup('family','ja3')) | summarize by src_ip, sni

objectives.title: Remote-monitoring tooling abuse check
objectives.falsification_criterion: If unmanaged AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installs are absent, RMM-based C2 is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: process | where name in ('anydesk.exe','teamviewer.exe','screenconnect.exe','atera*.exe') and signer != 'corp_managed'

hypotheses.title: Identity compromise of privileged users
hypotheses.statement: Privileged identities have been compromised through phishing, MFA fatigue, help-desk social engineering, or OAuth illicit-consent grants.
hypotheses.rationale: Archetype 'identity_compromise' selected based on CVEs cited: CVE-2026-62927, CVE-2026-63252, CVE-2026-58080; vectors: phishing, exploit, vpn-edge.

objectives.title: Impossible-travel / atypical sign-ins
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra ID / Okta risky-sign-in detections show no impossible-travel hits on privileged identities, account compromise is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: signin | where risk_level in ('high','medium') and user in (privileged_users) | summarize by country, ip

objectives.title: MFA-fatigue / push-bombing
objectives.falsification_criterion: If MFA telemetry shows no bursts of denied pushes followed by a successful one for the same user, MFA-fatigue compromise is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: mfa | summarize denies = countif(result=='deny'), accepts = countif(result=='accept') by user, bin(ts,1h) | where denies > 5 and accepts > 0

objectives.title: Help-desk social-engineering pivot
objectives.falsification_criterion: If ticketing / call-recording shows no recent password-reset or MFA-reset requests for privileged users without proper verification, help-desk vector is unsupported.
objectives.suggested_query: tickets | where action in ('password_reset','mfa_reset') and target in (privileged_users) | join (verifications) on ticket_id

objectives.title: OAuth illicit-consent grants
objectives.falsification_criterion: If Entra/Workspace audit logs show no recently consented third-party apps with high-impact scopes, OAuth abuse is disproven.
objectives.suggested_query: audit | where action == 'Consent to application' and scopes contains 'Mail.Read' or 'files.read.all'
